prose.text: - **The live round** is the block's `round` and `live` entries, fired by `gate.py run --live-legs --entry N`, one   drive at a time (step 11). The wrap never re-runs it; it re-verifies from `evidence/`. - **Non-priming probe:** `conductor preconditions --for real-model-interpretation` precedes every drive. It fires no   canary. There is no `boot` before any drive: it would prime the incident the drive's own canary dedupes against   (verification-harness.md 2026-08-19 (a)). - **Operator entries before the round** are fired once, by hand, in block order, and their results recorded in the   ledger: the Pulse git probes, the builds and their proofs, the env checks, the dir listing. `pulse-app` is launched   between them and the round (step 10); the agent starts it and stops it, on the overseer's word (inputs#I17). - **Smoke:** `status` is mint-then-read on `d3`'s `run_id`. - **The attempt ledger has no producing entry:** the agent authors it from the entries' recorded results and from   Pulse's own log, as every prior series' ledger was. The criteria that read it are held by the harvest   (`pre_registered` reads its digest line) and by the host-path probe. - **Night rule:** only the three `live` entries are GPU runs. Every other entry runs at any hour (inputs#I17). - **Pulse builds** run in the Pulse tree inside a subshell `cd`, because cargo reads its config from the cwd. - **Host paths:** every Pulse binary probe runs from inside `target/release` with bare file names; the model digest   entry prints the digest alone. Nothing an entry prints names a host path beyond what the gate tool respells. - **Controls owed at implement** (red before green, one-shot): step 12's `measured` table and step 13's temp-root   arms. Their readings go to the report.

prose.text: - **The live round** is the block's `round` and `live` entries, fired by `gate.py run --live-legs --entry N`, one   drive at a time (step 11). The wrap never re-runs it; it re-verifies from `evidence/`. - **Non-priming probe:** `conductor preconditions --for real-model-interpretation` precedes every drive. It fires no   canary. There is no `boot` before any drive: it would prime the incident the drive's own canary dedupes against   (verification-harness.md 2026-08-19 (a)). - **Operator entries before the round** are fired once, by hand, in block order, and their results recorded in the   ledger: the Pulse git probes, the builds and their proofs, the env checks, the dir listing. `pulse-app` is launched   between them and the round (step 10); the agent starts it and stops it, on the overseer's word (inputs#I17). - **Smoke:** `status` is mint-then-read on `d3`'s `run_id`. - **The attempt ledger has no producing entry:** the agent authors it from the entries' recorded results and from   Pulse's own log, as every prior series' ledger was. The criteria that read it are held by the harvest   (`pre_registered` reads its digest line) and by the host-path probe. - **Night rule:** only the three `live` entries are GPU runs. Every other entry runs at any hour (inputs#I17). - **Pulse builds** run in the Pulse tree inside a subshell `cd`, because cargo reads its config from the cwd. - **Host paths:** every Pulse binary probe runs from inside `target/release` with bare file names; the model digest   entry prints the digest alone. Nothing an entry prints names a host path beyond what the gate tool respells. - **Controls owed at implement** (red before green, one-shot): step 12's `measured` table and step 13's temp-root   arms. Their readings go to the report.
